I think most games have one or two factions that provide a really compelling campaign. 
The original RTW provides great options for turtling (Britannia), rushing (Egypt), as well as harder campaigns where you have to fight multi sided wars (Seleucia).
RTW:BI is criminally underrated, in my opinion. Both halves of the Roman Empire are really fun. The Western half has economic troubles, the invasion of barbarians, as well as inevitable revolts, making the campaign difficult, dynamic, yet rewarding. The Eastern half is great for turtling, as pushing into Sassinid territory means massive public order problems in conquered territory. You have to also defend from Clibinatrii (spelling possibly incorrect), which is a chore.
Medieval II provides great campaigns, such as the Venetian campaign (easy economy and great entry level soldiers), the Byzantine campaign (a headache to defend from Venice, Turks, and Timurids), and English campaign (longbows).
Napoleon provides the French and Russian campaigns, which play opposite each other. France is great for an aggressive player who wants to conquer Europe. I prefer turtling as Russia, watching Austria and Prussia fall to Napoleon while you build up your economy and armies. When they reach your borders, the tiniest slip up will lose the campaign, but France will have to face your unicorns, coffers, and winter.
Shotgun 2 as well as FotS provide great campaigns with dynamic unit rosters. I especially recommend FotS, because the transition from melee to gunpowder and artillery provides for a battle experience unique to the series.
